title: Categorize Products by SKU Pattern
description:
A warehouse stores SKUs in three canonical shapes. Classify every SKU and count products per category:
- **Standard** — two letters, dash, four digits (`^[A-Z]{2}-[0-9]{4}$`)
- **Bulk** — letters `B`, `K`, or `G` then a dash then three letters then a digit (`^[BKG]-[A-Z]{3}[0-9]$`)
- **Other** — anything else

Return columns `sku_type` (the literal strings `'Standard'`, `'Bulk'`, `'Other'`) and `product_count`, with one row per category that actually has products. Order by `sku_type` ascending.
solutionSql:
SELECT
  CASE
    WHEN REGEXP_LIKE(sku, '^[A-Z]{2}-[0-9]{4}$') THEN 'Standard'
    WHEN REGEXP_LIKE(sku, '^[BKG]-[A-Z]{3}[0-9]$') THEN 'Bulk'
    ELSE 'Other'
  END AS sku_type,
  COUNT(*) AS product_count
FROM products
GROUP BY sku_type
ORDER BY sku_type;
hint: Put REGEXP_LIKE inside a CASE expression in the SELECT, then GROUP BY the same CASE expression. Evaluate the Standard pattern before Bulk so unambiguous SKUs are caught first.
outputExplanation: AB-1234 is Standard. K-ABC9 starts with K and has three letters then a digit, so it is Bulk. 'B-AB12' has only two letters after the dash, 'XYZ-1' has no dash pattern, and '$k-abc7' is Other. The three groups are counted and returned.
